prompt: Two people edit the same wiki page; the second save silently overwrites the first person's changes.
why: Save with a version check; reject if the version changed.
trap: Each save is its own transaction; that doesn't stop this.

prompt: An API requires clients to send If-Match with the ETag they last read, and returns 412 if the resource changed.
trap: ETags here protect writes, not caching.

prompt: Stock is read as 1, two buyers each decrement it, and it ends at -1.
why: UPDATE ... WHERE version = ? (or WHERE stock > 0) so only one wins.

prompt: Conflicts on user settings are rare, and you don't want to hold row locks while users stare at a form for minutes.
tells: Conflicts on user settings are rare
why: Optimistic locking suits rare conflicts and long think times.
trap: Pessimistic locks would block for minutes.

prompt: A user edits a record offline for an hour; when they sync, the server should detect that someone else changed it meanwhile.
tells: edits a record offline for an hour
detect that someone else changed it
why: Send the version the edit was based on; reject or merge if it changed.
trap: A transaction can't stay open for an hour.

prompt: An update loop re-reads the row and retries when the version check fails, up to three times.
tells: retries when the version check fails
why: Read, modify, write with version, retry on conflict.

prompt: Instead of a version number, the update includes WHERE updated_at = the value read earlier.
tells: WHERE updated_at = the value read earlier
why: A timestamp works as the version (if precise enough).

prompt: A popular counter row gets thousands of updates a second, and almost every optimistic update fails and retries.
why: Optimistic locking is the wrong fit here: use atomic increments or shard the counter.
trap: Know when the pattern stops working.
